objective: Make project business permissions follow the selected project and its project roles while keeping system administration permissions global.
users: System administrators maintaining the permission catalog

requirements.statement: System settings must provide permission catalog maintenance instead of system role-to-permission assignment.
acceptance: Authorized administrators can query, create, edit, enable, disable and conditionally delete permissions
Permission codes are immutable after creation
counterexample: The system settings page still assigns business permissions directly to system roles

requirements.statement: Project roles must configure project business permissions from the central catalog.
acceptance: A project role drawer groups selectable permissions by menu
System permissions never appear as project role options
requirements.source: User request and confirmed design sections 1-2
counterexample: A project role can grant system settings access

requirements.statement: Effective business permissions must change with the active project and be enforced by the server.
acceptance: The same user receives different permissions for projects A and B according to assigned project roles
Menus, routes, buttons and protected APIs agree
Forged or mismatched project context is rejected
requirements.source: User request and confirmed design section 3
counterexample: Only frontend controls change while the backend still accepts unauthorized writes

requirements.statement: Existing project roles must be initialized without locking out project administration.
acceptance: PM roles receive all active project business permissions
Other existing roles receive active read permissions
Project owners retain full current-project permissions
counterexample: Migration leaves a project owner unable to configure roles

requirements.statement: Permission changes must preserve tenant and project isolation and be audited.
acceptance: Cross-tenant and cross-project role identifiers are rejected
Permission catalog and role assignment writes create audit records
counterexample: A role from one project can be assigned permissions through another project endpoint

invariants: Project roles cannot grant system permissions
Frontend visibility never replaces backend authorization
constraints: Keep existing Java packages and JWT format
Reuse sys_menu and sys_menu_permission as the permission catalog
Use X-Project-Id for request project context

selected_approach.name: Request-scoped project context with server-side permission union
selected_approach.reason: Provides immediate revocation, secure API enforcement and consistent project switching without token churn.

alternatives.name: Issue a new token on every project switch
alternatives.rejected_because: Creates token rotation and multi-tab consistency problems.

alternatives.name: Merge permissions only in the frontend

inside: Desktop and mobile role permission UI

components.name: System permission catalog
components.responsibility: Own permission definitions, lifecycle and reference protection.

components.name: Project role authorization
components.responsibility: Persist and validate role-permission selections within a project.

components.name: Security effective-permission resolver
components.responsibility: Union global system permissions with active-project business permissions and build routes.

components.name: Frontend project/auth context
components.responsibility: Attach project context, refresh permissions/routes and recover failed switches.

interfaces.name: Permission catalog API
interfaces.contract: Tenant-scoped active catalog with immutable codes and reference-safe lifecycle.

interfaces.name: Project role permissions API
interfaces.contract: GET and transactionally replace permissions for a role belonging to the path project.

interfaces.name: Effective auth context
interfaces.contract: Global system permissions plus active-project business permissions after membership and tenant validation.

transitions: keep project A active while loading
data_flows.output: Navigation and protected actions reflect project B

data_flows.input: Project owner saves role permission IDs
data_flows.output: Subsequent requests use the new permission set

error_handling.condition: Missing, malformed or mismatched project context
error_handling.recovery: Select a valid accessible project and retry.

error_handling.behavior: Keep the previous project and permissions; show a retryable error.
error_handling.recovery: Retry without losing the current page context.

error_handling.behavior: Keep the drawer and local selection open; do not show success.
error_handling.recovery: Correct the validation error or retry.

error_handling.behavior: Reject deletion and identify that the permission is in use.
error_handling.recovery: Remove assignments or disable the permission.

verification_strategy.signal: Catalog and project-role UI/API operations persist and enforce allowed scope.
verification_strategy.method: Focused backend tests, frontend build and browser acceptance.

verification_strategy.signal: Project A/B produce different effective permissions and forged contexts return 403.
verification_strategy.method: Security integration tests and real API calls.

verification_strategy.signal: Migration output assigns all/read/none according to role type and owner remains privileged.
verification_strategy.method: Flyway migration test and seeded-database queries.

assumptions.text: Every project business write can be associated with one current project.
assumptions.basis: Existing project-scoped tables and top project selector.
assumptions.falsifier: An in-scope endpoint performs a cross-project operation without a single owner project.

assumptions.text: Project role code PM identifies the manager role in existing data.
assumptions.basis: Current project access and security queries already use role_code = PM.
assumptions.falsifier: Existing projects use a different manager role code.

unknowns.question: Which legacy project API calls currently omit project context outside path/query data?
unknowns.impact: Implementation plan must inventory and adapt those callers.

unknowns.question: Why does the local plugin entry checker receive an unknown error from the Codex plugin list?
unknowns.impact: Repository development-entry gate must pass before product code implementation.

decisions.decision: Keep system administration permissions global and restrict project roles to project business permissions.
decisions.reason: Prevents project-level privilege elevation into platform administration.

decisions.decision: Initialize PM with all permissions, other existing roles with read permissions, new roles with none, and owners with full fallback.
decisions.reason: Provides a usable migration without broad write access.

decisions.decision: Use request-scoped project context and server-side permission union.
decisions.reason: Secure, immediately consistent and avoids token churn.

decisions.decision: Use central permission maintenance and a fullscreen-capable project-role drawer.
decisions.reason: Separates catalog ownership from per-project assignment while reusing established UI patterns.

risks.mitigation: Inventory calls, classify global versus project APIs and add contract tests before switching enforcement.

risks.risk: Routes and API checks use different permission sources.
risks.impact: Visible pages fail or hidden pages remain callable.
risks.mitigation: Use one effective-permission resolver and test route/button/API agreement.
Seed only active read actions for non-PM roles and verify counts per project.

approval.evidence: User confirmed all three design sections and selected the recommended request-scoped approach.
